top_10.title: Check required inputs before long agent runs
top_10.body:
## Problem

Long agent runs can start without all required inputs. Text may arrive while images or other attachments do not.

The run can then complete against incomplete evidence.

Katie Parrott’s [early-access Fable 5.2 review](https://every.to/vibe-check/fable-5-2) reports an overnight agent run that analyzed slide text but missed deck screenshots. This is an observation, not an independently verified benchmark.

## Change

Add a preflight that inventories required inputs before a long EGM run begins.

The preflight must confirm that the agent can read each required input. It must distinguish text, images, and other attachments.

Stop the run with an actionable error when a required input is absent or unreadable.

## Acceptance criteria

- The run defines its required inputs before execution.
- The preflight confirms the count, type, and identity of each input.
- The preflight verifies that the agent can read each input.
- The run stops before execution when a required input is absent or unreadable.
- The run records the preflight result.
- Automated tests cover text-only input, mixed text and images, a missing image, and an unreadable attachment.

top_10.title: Flaky: test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt (fixed 60 ms sleep before reading flushed frame)
top_10.body:
`test/test_subagent_scale_batch.py::TestCoalescer::test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt` failed on an unrelated PR.

- Run: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/41797479802/job/126467561880 (PR #29490, head 712e6f822c65)
- OS: ubuntu, Python 3.12, Backend Tests shard 3
- Failing line: `((etype, data),) = all_frames` -> `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)`

The test waits a fixed `await asyncio.sleep(0.06)` past the 20 ms flush tick and then expects one frame. On a slow runner the flush has not happened yet, so the list is empty. It passes 8/8 locally (alone and with the whole file under -n 4). PR #29490 does not touch the coalescer or this test.

Likely fix: wait for the frame (poll with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

top_10.title: Church name text hidden in sidebar but still shown on login page when a custom logo is uploaded
top_10.body:
## Description When a custom church logo is uploaded (Admin → System → Church Information), the church-name text is hidden in the sidebar but still shown on the login page — inconsistent behavior across the two surfaces that both render the logo. - **Sidebar** (`src/Include/Header.php`, lines ~186-199): the `navbar-brand-text` span is wrapped in `if (ChurchLogoService::hasCustomLogo())` — it only renders when there's **no** custom logo: ```php 'navbar-brand-image crm-brand-logo']) ?> ... ``` - **Login page** (`src/session/templates/begin-session.php`, lines 30-37): `ChurchLogo::img()` and `ChurchMetaData::getChurchName()` render unconditionally as separate elements, with no `hasCustomLogo()` check at all: ```php

``` Confirmed identical on both `master` and the `7.8.1` tag (same blob SHA on `begin-session.php` across both refs). The sidebar's hide-on-custom-logo behavior was intentional per #9719 ("The uploaded logo replaces the ChurchCRM branding in the sidebar (where it also hides the church-name text)") on the assumption that an uploaded logo already contains the church name as artwork. The login page not following the same rule means that assumption isn't applied consistently — admins who want the name visible lose it in the sidebar but keep it on login, with no way to choose. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Admin → System → Church Information → upload a custom logo. 2. Visit the dashboard — sidebar shows only the logo, no church name. 3. Log out and view the login page — logo **and** church name are both shown. ## Expected Consistent behavior between the sidebar and the login page — either both hide the name when a custom logo is present, or neither does. ## Reported by maestrovivo, in the project's Discord #support-chat.

issues.title: HLSL output writes the `length()` of a `buffer float*` helper parameter as `v.length()`, which DXC rejects
Docs: stale statements about the chat screen, dictation and image intake found in the chat-ui test campaign
issues.body:
The chat-ui test campaign (PR #741) found these while checking what the docs say against the code. Line numbers are at the campaign's merge base.

- [ ] **rag-design.md ~:666** names a `scopeChipLabel` helper that does not exist; the "Answering from" label is computed inline in `ScopePopover.tsx` (~:240-280).
- [x] **rag-design.md §15.5 / §15.7 (~:2458-2464, ~:2539)** still describe the pre-D69 meter: a "Context: 6.4k / 8k" tooltip and a progressbar with `aria-valuetext`. Today it is a `role="meter"` labelled "Memory" with a "… % full (about 6.4k of 8k tokens)" tooltip (`ContextMeter.tsx`). (PR #776: both now describe the `role="meter"` "Memory" meter and its bands)
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:2377** (Voice dictation) says the "not installed" mic deep-links with `onNavigate('models')`; since #527 it is `models:voice` (`ChatScreen.tsx` ~:2681).
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:12739** (Image understanding §5) says decode "re-encodes to the input MIME"; since #124 a WEBP becomes PNG (`decode.ts` `outputMimeFor`, ~:111; §11 already says so).
- [ ] **Code comments:** `renderer/lib/displayMap.ts` ~:146-148 repeats the "lands on an odd index" claim that #741 corrected in AssistantMarkdown (with one capture group the split always ends on prose), and `shared/citation-markers.ts` ~:18 and displayMap say `normalizeMathDelimiters` lives in Transcript.tsx (it is in AssistantMarkdown.tsx).
- [x] **ChatScreen.tsx ~:1834-1836**: the stream `finally` comment promises the "Stopped" toast only when no error explained the early end; the condition never reads the error (see #742). (PR #776: the condition now reads `sendSucceeded`, and the comment says why)

issues.title: Audit 2026-11: contract, SKILL.md, references, README and process docs disagree with the code
issues.body:
From a full audit of the tree at 47a962a (3.5.0 + #452) on 2026-11-12. Each finding was checked against the code, reproduced where it can be run, and then checked again by a second reviewer who tried to refute it. Findings that were refuted, already decided in `docs/design-decisions.md`, or already filed are left out. The severity is the second reviewer's. The reproduction and suggested fix for each one are in the audit record (ask on this issue to have one posted).

**26 findings: 0 high, 7 medium, 19 low.** Tick a box and name the PR when a fix is merged.

Contract, SKILL.md and references:

- [ ] **medium** `SKILL.md:109` (A191): Two SKILL.md routing rows give commands that fail on every input: `fit.py --duration 2x` and `background.py` without --width/--height
- [ ] **medium** `docs/contract.md:225` (A197): docs/contract.md's role, verification-policy and visual-check tables still describe a 21-tool subset; "requires_visual_verification is true exactly for" names 8 tools, while the JSON and its test have 27
- [ ] **medium** `references/workflow.md:35` (A192): workflow.md and gotchas.md still say scenes.py refuses audio-only input; since 3.2.0 it measures it (README and the contract say so)
- [ ] **medium** `scripts/_contract.py:240` (A193): metadata.py --auto-chapters and probe.py --analyze run ffmpeg under --dry-run, but the contract says ffmpeg_execution "none" and every dry-run list leaves them out
- [ ] **medium** `scripts/graphics.py:1` (A202): graphics.py --dry-run on an input an earlier step will write fails with a misleading "--end must be after --start"; the other tools plan it
- [ ] **low** `references/ci-platform-pitfalls.md:206` (A200): The drawtext-crash remedy "pass --font-file explicitly" names a flag look.py, scenes.py and grid.py do not have
- [ ] **low** `references/flags.md:12` (A201): The shared-flag claims are not true of every script: verify.py's --timeout defaults to 600 (per step), not 1800, and six tools take no -o
- [ ] **low** `references/gotchas.md:211` (A199): workflow.md and gotchas.md prescribe `--lang ja|ko` (or brand.json "lang") for Han-only text, but overlay.py has neither and draws Japanese Han text with a Simplified Chinese face
- [ ] **low** `scripts/_contract.py:181` (A196): PR #452: `silence.py --transcribe` with a sentence flag needs a speech engine and runs it under --dry-run, but capabilities, error_reasons and model_downloads still say only `--filler --transcribe`
- [ ] **low** `scripts/_contract.py:792` (A194): output_schema leaves out keys tools emit, including cropdetect's main result `crop`, though docs/contract.md documents several of them
- [ ] **low** `scripts/_contract.py:1680` (A195): The tool `description` in the contract and in MCP tools/list is cut mid-sentence for 17 tools
- [ ] **low** `scripts/_contract.py:2034` (A198): The contract's error_kinds descriptions are narrower than the code: missing_tool also covers encoder, decoder and ASR engines, and verification is raised by loudness, join --copy and the render pack

README, CHANGELOG, roadmap and process docs:

- [ ] **medium** `.claude/skills/release-management/SKILL.md:133` (A205): release-management skill note says the repo has no release.yml and that releases are cut by hand
- [ ] **medium** `README.md:353` (A203): README gives contract_version as 1.0; the contract emits 2.0, and docs/contract.md and README's own Stability section say 2.0
- [ ] **low** `.claude/skills/code-review/references/result-honesty.md:57` (A208): code-review skill lists probe as analysis_only and leaves out overlay, naming DRY_RUN_ANALYSIS as the source
- [ ] **low** `.claude/skills/cross-surface-changes/SKILL.md:214` (A207): Other skill notes give stale tool counts, test locations and CI commands
- [ ] **low** `.claude/skills/destructive-operations/SKILL.md:203` (A206): Repo notes in destructive-operations and github-actions report defects that the tree has fixed
- [ ] **low** `CHANGELOG.md:2107` (A215): CHANGELOG has two '## 1.15.0' headings; release-note extraction takes only the first, three-line one
- [ ] **low** `CONTRIBUTING.md:24` (A216): '25 single-input tools' is 24 tools (cut appears twice); the sweep table also leaves out single-file tools while claiming to cover them all
- [ ] **low** `CONTRIBUTING.md:116` (A204): CONTRIBUTING says nothing in CI publishes the MCP Registry entry; since 3.5.0 release.yml publishes it
- [ ] **low** `README.md:199` (A209): README and contract.md say a fake-ffmpeg test runs every tool under --dry-run; it runs 17, and the fake binary applies to about 9
- [ ] **low** `README.md:226` (A211): #451 and #452's silence flags reached scripts.md, contract.md and demos but not the README or SKILL.md that CONTRIBUTING requires
- [ ] **low** `README.md:471` (A212): README says only `silence --filler --transcribe` runs the speech engine under --dry-run; #452 adds `--transcribe` with the sentence flags
- [ ] **low** `README.md:673` (A210): README names two Windows-skipped tests and says 'everything else' runs on Windows; test_contract.py skips more than a dozen
- [ ] **low** `README.md:675` (A213): README says a PR never needs to touch CHANGELOG.md; CONTRIBUTING requires it for a feat, and a test fails a PR that closes an issue without it
- [ ] **low** `docs/roadmap.md:231` (A214): Roadmap describes a never-shipped look.py --best-frame under a 'shipped + evaluated' heading and stops at 2.0.0; design-decisions says every version is marked

issues.title: fix(ci): migrate reusable eval workflows to the Go CLI and require real automatic-run artifacts
issues.body:
## Summary

<!-- 2-4 sentences: describe the bug, feature request, documentation gap, or task. -->

The reusable `waza.yaml` workflow still installs a Python package and uses obsolete CLI/result contracts, while automatic `waza-eval.yml` runs do not resolve output defaults before execution. A successful current-main automatic evaluation run uploaded no result artifact. Migrate retained consumer workflows and examples to one tested Go CLI contract; proposed target v0.41.0.

## Type of issue

- [x] Bug
- [ ] Feature request
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Maintenance
- [ ] Question or investigation

## Agent instructions

<!-- Make this actionable for a coding agent. Include constraints, likely files, and what not to change. -->

- Goal: Every advertised reusable workflow invokes the actual Go Waza contract, preserves meaningful failures, and produces usable evidence on push/PR/dispatch/call events.
- In scope: Installation/source-version strategy, supported arguments, effective input defaults, result/output mapping, artifact verification, and corresponding CI guide/site examples.
- Out of scope: Reintroducing Python Waza, altering product exit/reporting policies to accommodate stale examples, silently changing callers' output names, or using mutable latest installs as exact-source regression evidence.
- Likely files or areas: `.github/workflows/waza.yaml`, `waza-eval.yml`, `skills-ci-example.yml`, `docs/CI-CD-GUIDE.md`, site CI documentation and workflow contract tests.
- Dependencies or related issues: Coordinate final enforcement with [#900](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/900). Keep reporter product bug [#892](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/892) separate; this issue fixes workflow consumption and result evidence, not the reporter implementation.

## Current behavior

<!-- What happens today? For bugs, include the actual result and error output if available. -->

[`waza.yaml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza.yaml#L48-L81) runs `pip install waza`, `--format json`, `--fail-threshold`, `waza report`, and reads `.summary.pass_rate` / `.summary.composite_score`. Current Go run accepts `default` or `github-comment` output format and writes native summary fields such as `success_rate`; there is no corresponding `cmd_report.go` command. In [`waza-eval.yml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza-eval.yml#L154-L197), `OUTPUT_FILE` reads a raw input that is empty on automatic events, but upload falls back to `results.json`. [Current-main run 41918346222](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222) succeeded, warned `No files were found with the provided path: results.json`, and its artifacts API returned an empty list. The CI guide repeats obsolete summary keys/actions, so documentation can propagate the mismatch.

<!-- What should happen instead? For feature requests, describe the desired outcome. -->

Resolve effective defaults once for all event types and use the same values for execution, parsing, summary, and upload. Use a reviewed Go installation/build strategy with genuine embedded dashboard assets where source builds require them. Validate result shape, completeness, and availability instead of interpreting null/missing values as zero or success. Preserve documented reusable inputs/outputs through migration or explicitly document reviewed breaking changes.

## Steps to reproduce

2. Read the current-main automatic run log's artifact warning.
3. Query `GET /repos/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222/artifacts` and compare the empty list with the workflow's stated result-artifact contract.

## Environment

- OS: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu.
- Waza version or commit: `f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c`.
- Go version: CI specifies 1.26; stale reusable workflow provisions Python 3.11.

## Acceptance criteria

issues.title: [Request] 文档：Secure Boot 开启下的自签流程（db 自签 / MOK+shim）与三个已知坑
issues.body:
> 起草说明：本文由 AI 辅助整理，事实来自仓库现状与 #145 的讨论；**没有做真机验证**（我这台没有可切 Secure Boot 的独显机位），凡未实测之处都已标注。若与现场不符，以现场为准。

### 建议类型 / Request type

文档修正 / Documentation change

### 当前问题与需求 / Current problem and need

**要解决的是文档缺口，不是功能缺口。** 想让 Secure Boot 保持开启的用户，现在在文档里只能读到一句：

- `docs/faq.md:272` / `docs/faq.en.md:263`：`替换 U 盘启动文件前先备份。Secure Boot 关闭或使用受信任的自签 EFI。`

这句话承认了自签这条路存在，但没有过程。而 [#145](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/145)（已关闭）里三条路只写全了一条：

| #145 里的方案 | 文档状态 |
|---|---|
| 方案一 休眠切换法（SB 开/关来回切） | 评论里有完整流程，未入 FAQ |
| 方案二 固件内置 FFS（PR #100） | `docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162` 有可行性，标注【待实证】 |
| 方案三 MOK + shim | 评论里有六步，未入 FAQ |
| 方案三 db 自签 | **只有"简版"一句**：每台机器手动导证书、每次更新重签 |

而现场反馈指向的恰恰是最后这条：#145 里有一条西语报告——"Conseguí firmar con un certificado propio el Efi, de modo que ha sido posible iniciar con el secure boot activado"（用自己的证书签了 EFI，因此可以在 Secure Boot 开启下启动）。这是 db 自签路线**可用**的现场证据，但它现在埋在一条已关闭的 issue 的评论区里，既没进 FAQ，也没进兼容性记录。

现实需求面也不小：#145 的原始动机是打 LoL/Vanguard（反作弊要求 SB 开启），而 `docs/community-reports.md` 里的实测行几乎每条都写着 "Secure Boot off"——SB-on 场景目前是文档空白区。

补充一点定位：这**不是**在申请"绕过 Secure Boot"。自签属 `SECURITY.md:53` 威胁模型里"已开启 Secure Boot 且已导入自签证书"的合法配置，与方案一、方案二并列，只是缺文档。

### 期望改进 / Desired improvement

新增 `docs/faq.md#secureboot`（EN 同步 `docs/faq.en.md`）一节，建议内容：

1. **两条路线对比表**：db 自签（固件直接验你的签名，代价是每台导证 + 每次重签）vs MOK+shim（不动 db，走发行版 shim）。shim 那条直接链接 #145 现有六步，不重复写。
2. **db 自签五步**：
   - 生成密钥/证书（`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -addext "extendedKeyUsage=codeSigning"`——这个 EKU 不能省，Windows 侧 `signtool` 会校验）；
   - 签名与验证（`sbsign --key ... --cert ... --output ...`；`sbverify --cert ...`；Windows 等价物 `signtool sign /fd SHA256` + `signtool verify /pa`）；
   - 把 **DER 证书追加**进 db 的三种方式：固件 Key Management（`db → Append / Append from file`）、`efitools` 的 `efi-updatevar -a -c cert.crt -k KEK.key db`、`sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft`（`--microsoft` 才会把微软证书一并写回）；
   - 新版 maker 直接吃签名后的件：`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284`（`-BootEfi`）、`:488`（盘根）、`:494`（`EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`），即
     ```powershell
     .\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family ad102 -Out G:\ -BootEfi .\BOOTX64.signed.efi
     ```
   - 验证：`mokutil --sb-state` 应为 `SecureBoot enabled`；固件层真正放行的铁证是盘上出现新的 `loader.log` 且含 `TX BUILD` banner。
3. **三条硬纪律**（这部分比签名本身更容易出事）：
   - **只能追加，不能替换 db 里的微软证书**——`bootmgfw.efi` 靠 *Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011* 签名，删了 Windows 起不来；
   - **动 PK 前先导出 PK/KEK/db 备份**；若板子要求清 PK 进 Setup Mode 才能 Append，事后必须把原厂证书恢复并重新 enroll PK；
   - **私钥只留本机**：db 里一旦有你的证书，这把私钥就能给这台机器签任何引导组件。
4. **三个已知坑**：
   - **SB 开着时 `ssdiag` 仍然不可用**：它临时加载的 `pmxdrv.sys` 是 Intel/COMODO 2018 交叉签名、无微软根，SB-ON 必然被 DSE 拒（`tools/ssdiag/README.md` 的 "Secure Boot — the gate that actually refuses this driver"、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`）。所以 SB 常开的机器上，系统内读回只能走 `loader.log` 的 `HANDOFF-OUT`（EFI 阶段零驱动读回）或 Linux 侧 `tools/diag-unlock.py`；要 `ssdiag --reapply` 修回锁，仍须临时关一次 SB。
   - **BitLocker / PCR[7]**：SB 或 db 状态变化会改 PCR[7]，可能弹恢复密钥，操作前先挂起保护。
   - **换版本必须重签**，签名后再改一个字节即失效；资产 `*.bin` 不需要签名（SB 只验 PE 引导链）。
5. **反作弊边界**（与 #145 的警告保持一致）：db 自签不改 SB 状态位，Vanguard（LoL）通常可过；ACE 系（腾讯）会校验 TPM/PCR[7] 链式启动记录，自签链的度量与原厂引导不同，**不保证过检**——打 ACE 系游戏请回到方案一。

顺带把 `docs/faq.md:272` / `.en.md:263` 那句改成带锚点的链接。

### 相关版本、文档与参考资料 / Versions, documentation and references

- 文档现状：`docs/faq.md:272`、`docs/faq.en.md:263`（自签仅一句）
- 讨论：#145（休眠切换法、FFS 方案、MOK+shim 六步、db 自签简版）；西语现场反馈在该 issue 评论中
- 固件形态可行性：`docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162`（SB 只验 OS 引导链）
- maker 的 boot 路径改动：`5684752`（打印可执行 copy 步骤）、`c0f3518`（输出不再纯平铺）、`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284/488/494/500/505-511`
- ssdiag 的 SB 门：`tools/ssdiag/README.md`、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`
- 威胁模型定位：`SECURITY.md:53`
- FAQ 判据/回锁值（本 issue 不涉及，仅说明读回路径不同）：`docs/faq.md:189`、`docs/cold-values.md:139`

### 替代方案与补充信息 / Alternatives and additional context

- **替代**：维持现状，让每个 SB-on 用户自己在 Discussions 问一遍。现状的代价是 #145 已经被关掉，新来的人搜不到过程。
- **更小的一步**：只把这份内容作为 #145 的补充评论贴回去——但该单已关闭，不解决"下次还能找到吗"。
- **我愿意直接出 patch**：如果维护者认可，可以照 #141 / #144 的方式提 docs PR，中英同步、只动 `docs/faq*.md`。
- **缺一个现场字段**：能否请 #145 那位西语报告者补 **主板型号** 与 **`ssdiag` 是否被拒**（第 4 条里"必然被拒"还是"通常被拒"取决于此），以及 **BitLocker 是否弹过恢复密钥**。这三项决定文档该写成硬性结论还是保守表述。

issues.title: [Report] RTX 4060 Laptop (28A0) / MECHREVO Yaoshi15Pro 2024 (GM5IX0A, i7-14650HX) - v2.1.9 TX success, matched A/B FP16 +81%, 15-inch thin laptop @ 140 W
issues.body:
## 摘要 / Summary

`10de:28a0`（AD107 · 24 SM · 8 GB）在机械革命 **耀世15Pro 2024**（i7-14650HX / 32 GB）上完成 **v2.1.9 Ada 事务**，EFI 侧读回全绿（`HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff`），Windows 正常进入。

**平台定位需要先说明**：这是一台 **15 寸轻薄游戏本**，不是同 TGP 的厚砖机。140 W 塞进这个厚度的机身，散热余量本来就是这个形态的短板——下面的 87 ℃ / 2.5 GHz 持续数据要放在这个前提下看，不代表其他 140 W 机型的水平。

同一脚本、同一 GPU 设置（140 W / 核心 +105 MHz / 显存 +200 MHz）的前后对照：

| 路径 | 解锁前 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.26 / 21.27 | **38.45** | **+81%** |
| BF16 | 21.25 / 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 / 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3 | 40.79 / 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（对照） | 6.41 / 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

绝对值比 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）和 [#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882）低 13–15%，实测受 **140 W 功耗墙 + 87 ℃ 温度墙**限制（持续负载下核心 2625 → 2430 MHz），与这台 15 寸轻薄机身的散热包络相符。新增信息：28a0 的首份**同脚本匹配 A/B**，以及解锁态下的持续功耗/时钟/温度采样。

---

## 工具版本 / Tool version

- **nv-uefi-unlocker v2.1.9** 官方发布包，未做任何本地修改
- `BOOTX64.EFI` 335,872 B，SHA-256 `9D2C41F90B290AD0DA3ECF294016A7EA67638E2625D8E1B1735028298943BB5C`（与 [#35](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/35) 记录的官方 v2.1.9 同一文件）
- 资产：`-Family 40` 生成的 `ad102` family 共 8 个文件，`loader.log` 中逐个 `TX-ASSET-DIAG: ... loaded N/N bytes` 全量校验通过
- 未使用 `i_know_what_i_am_doing.txt` / `tx-quiet.txt` / `tx-select-bdf.txt` / `tx-require-d0.txt` 等任何 marker（日志中均为 `absent`）

## GPU 与平台 / GPU and platform

- **GPU**：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU，AD107，24 SM，8192 MiB
- **PCI ID**：`10DE:28A0`，子系统 `139A:1D05`（机械革命），地址 `0000:01:00.0`；音频功能 `10de:22be @ 01:00.1`
- **VBIOS**：`95.07.3f.00.26`　**驱动**：596.49（WDDM）
- **整机**：MECHREVO **耀世15Pro 2024**（Yaoshi15Pro Series GM5IX0A），**15 寸轻薄游戏本**；Intel Core i7-14650HX；内存 32 GB
- **BIOS**：American Megatrends International `N.1.05MRO06`（2024-01-30）
- **OS**：Windows 11 Pro build 26200
- **显示拓扑**：**独显直连**，内屏由 dGPU 驱动，2560×1440 @ 240 Hz；Intel UHD Graphics 存在于系统中但无显示输出（`CM_PROB_PHANTOM`），无 eGPU、无第二块独立显卡
- **功耗档**：机械革命电竞控制台「狂飙」档，`ConfigurableTGPSwitch=1 / ConfigurableTGPTarget=140`、Dynamic Boost 开关关闭（值 25）、核心 +105 MHz、显存 +200 MHz；实测 `power.draw` 峰值 139.8 W
- **启动方式**：UEFI，AMI F7 一次性启动菜单，FAT32 U 盘（VendorCo ProductCode，MBR，63 GB 中划 30 GB 分区）
- **Secure Boot**：事务时**已关闭**（当前仍未恢复）；**CSM / ReBAR：未检查**

## 操作过程 / Procedure

1. 在目标机（本机）解压 v2.1.9 发布包，管理员 PowerShell 运行 `.\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family 40`，自动识别本机为 40 系并只生成 `ad102` 资产；`NVIDIA-kernel-module-source-610.43.03` 与 `nvidia-utils-610.43.03` 两个钉版输入按脚本校验通过
2. 把脚本列出的 7 个 `.bin` 复制到 U 盘根目录，`BOOTX64.EFI` 放入 `EFI/BOOT/`
3. BIOS 中关闭 Secure Boot；从系统「重启」→ F7 一次性菜单选 `UEFI: VendorCo ProductCode 1.00, Partition 1`
4. 版本屏按 **空格** 确认（无 armed marker，走 30 秒超时语义）
5. 事务完成后自动链回 Windows，未修改 NVRAM 永久启动顺序
6. 全程只尝试了这一次事务，无重试、无断电恢复过程

## EFI 执行结果 / EFI execution result

```
TX: ===== target 1/1: 10de:28a0 @ 0000:01:00.0 =====
TX: device 10de:28a0 -> asset family 'ad102'
TX: V67 present - unlock mode (family-specific write chain)
TX: BEGIN (phases: detach claim pre-flr scrub gfw layout fwsec booter verify selectors restore flr)
TX: >4GB staging gate: false (family ad102)
TX: detach+claim ok
POST-BOOT: FEAT_PLM=0xffffffff SS0=0x161166 SS1=0x5
POST-BOOT: FACTORY FEAT_READOUT_1=0x00410080 (0 = full speed; badf5040 = PLM still closed)
POST-BOOT: SEC2 MAILBOX0=0x67b00001 WPR2_HI=0x1ffae00
POST-BOOT: WPRCFG=0xfffff0ff FBPA=0xffffff0f WPR=0xffffffff
SELECTOR RESULT: SS0=0x88888888 SS1=0x8
POST-FLR: GFW halted the cores
POST-FLR: WPR2=0x1ffffe00/0x0
POST-FLR: verified (selectors survive AON)
RECONNECT: ConnectController ok (recursive=true)          ← 默认 recursive=true，未跳过重连
FINAL: transaction complete, all DMA released
SELECTOR RESULT: transaction complete
HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff wpr2_hi=0x0
             pmcsr=0x0008 dstate=D0 | tu10x: ... | tu10x_unlock=false ss0_unlock=true ss1_unlock=true plm_open=true
CHAIN-PRE: start-time PE header probe ok - StartImage the preloaded '\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi'
```

阶段时序（`[+ms]` 前缀）：CONFIRM 262ms → 空格 14527ms → 事务本体 19300ms 起 → FINAL 22704ms → CHAIN 22799ms。

补充读回：事务前采样的 `SAMPLE FEAT_READOUT_1 = 0x00410080` 与 `POST-BOOT: FACTORY FEAT_READOUT_1=0x00410080` 一致，与本仓 [cold-values.md](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/blob/main/docs/cold-values.md) 已载的 AD107 出厂值逐位相同（九个 3 位字段中 #2/#5/#7 = 2），解锁后 `HANDOFF-OUT` 读到 `0x00000000`——与既有 AD107 冷值表吻合，不构成新数据点。

## 系统内验证 / In-OS verification

- Windows 正常启动，`bootmgfw` 链回成功，无 Code 12、无黑屏、无 TDR
- 驱动 596.49 正常加载，`nvidia-smi` 列出 GPU 于 `00000000:01:00.0`，P0，`Disp.A On`（独显直连持有显示）
- PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 正常运算，所有基准正确性检查 PASS
- **ssdiag：未通过，因此独立寄存器读回未验证。** 具体输出：

```
PLATFORM: vulnerable-driver blocklist = OFF
PLATFORM: core isolation (HVCI)       = unknown (value absent - the Windows default applies)
PLATFORM: Secure Boot                 = OFF
NOTE: a signed kernel driver is installed for the duration of the probe; ...
StartService failed: win32 31
```

  `SSDIAG_PMXDRV` 服务已成功安装（System 日志 7045，`\??\C:\Users\...\Temp\ssdiag-pmxdrv.sys`），但启动返回 `ERROR_GEN_FAILURE`。HVCI 场景键在本机注册表中不存在、VBS 未启用，**看起来不是代码完整性拦截**，暂按 [#40](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/40) 说的「平台拒绝 vs 驱动不能干活」两类形态无法区分，尚未复跑。系统侧状态目前仅由 EFI `HANDOFF-OUT` 读回 + 吞吐签名两方面佐证。

## 原始证据 / Raw evidence

- 完整 `loader.log`（433 行 / 40,719 B）见文末折叠块，未经修改
- `tools/collect_compat.py` 输出：`gpus=2 fields=46 verdicts=15`，`10de:28a0` 判为 `ad102 (Ada)`。注意它把音频功能 `10de:22be` 也列成了一个 GPU 条目（两条记录字段完全相同），不确定是否符合预期
- 无 NVIDIA 固件、无 BitLocker 密钥、无序列号；`loader.log` 已按 CONTRIBUTING 要求检查过

## 性能对比 / Performance comparison

**口径**：`make-usbroot.ps1` 自带前的自写脚本 `gemm_bench.py`（`torch.mm`，8192 系尺寸扫，`cudaEvent` 计时，每尺寸 5 次预热 + 3 窗口 × 20 次取中位），**解锁前后同脚本、同 GPU 设置**；解锁前为上一次启动（stock），解锁后为事务后同一次启动，两次测量间隔约 40 分钟，期间未改任何 GPU 设置。

**A/B（N=4096，TF/s）**

| 路径 | stock 第1次 | stock 第2次 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.27 | 21.26 | **38.45** | +81% |
| BF16 | 21.25 | 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 | 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3（`_scaled_mm`） | 40.79 | 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（TF32 off，对照） | 6.41 | 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 153.0 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

`FP16 / FP8` 比值：stock 0.52 → 解锁后 0.51；`FP16 / FP32` 比值：stock 3.1× → 解锁后 5.9×。三条对照（FP32、显存带宽、以及时钟本身）都持平，说明增益不是时钟或散热瞬态造成的。

issues.title: First time contributing? Start here.
issues.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

issues.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
issues.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

issues.title: Use package-relative imports to avoid collisions with user code
issues.body:
Hi @MarshalX et al! First off, thanks for building and maintaining this library. It's great!

When I first tried it just now, I immediately hit an `ImportError`. I have an `atproto_firehose.py` module in my project's root, and atproto doesn't use package-relative imports, so it tried to import its own `atproto_firehose`, got mine instead, and choked:

```
ImportError: Failed to import test module: test_atproto_firehose
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.11/3.11.9/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.11/lib/python3.11/unittest/loader.py", line 162, in loadTestsFromName
    module = __import__(module_name)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/ryan/src/bridgy-fed/tests/test_atproto_firehose.py", line 28, in <module>
    import atproto_firehose
  File "/Users/ryan/src/bridgy-fed/atproto_firehose.py", line 27, in <module>
    from atproto import CAR, AtUri, FirehoseSubscribeReposClient, firehose_models, models, parse_subscribe_repos_message
  File "/Users/ryan/src/bridgy-fed/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/atproto/__init__.py", line 11, in <module>
```

issues.title: Session.decode silently misparses truncated 5-field session strings via 4-field fallback
issues.body:
## Description

`Session.decode()` has a backward-compatibility path that accepts 4-field session strings (the old format). When a **5-field** session string is truncated (e.g., to 50% of its length), it can produce exactly 4 `:::`-separated segments if the truncation point falls between the 3rd and 4th separator. In that case, the SDK silently accepts the corrupted string via the old-format code path, producing a `Session` with correct `handle`, `did`, and `access_jwt` but a **garbage `refresh_jwt`**.

The resulting client appears fully functional — `Client.login(session_string=corrupted)` succeeds and API calls work — until the access token expires and refresh fails with an opaque error.

## Reproduction

```python
from atproto_client import Session

# Simulate a 5-field session string with asymmetric JWT lengths
short_jwt = "eyJ" + "A" * 300   # access_jwt
long_jwt = "eyJ" + "B" * 800    # refresh_jwt
session_str = ":::".join([
    "test.bsky.social",           # handle
    "did:plc:abc123",             # did
    short_jwt,                    # access_jwt
    long_jwt,                     # refresh_jwt
    "https://bsky.social",        # pds_endpoint
])

# Truncate to 50% — lands between 3rd and 4th separator
corrupted = session_str[: len(session_str) // 2]
fields = corrupted.split(":::")
assert len(fields) == 4  # Matches old-format path!

s = Session.decode(corrupted)
# s.handle and s.did are correct
# s.access_jwt is the FULL original access token
# s.refresh_jwt is a truncated fragment of the real refresh token
# s.pds_endpoint is the default (https://bsky.social) — real endpoint is lost
```

## Root cause

In `Session.decode()`:

```python
if len(fields) == 4:
    # Old session format
    handle, did, access_jwt, refresh_jwt = fields
    return cls(handle, did, access_jwt, refresh_jwt)
```

The 4-field path doesn't validate that the fields contain plausible values (e.g., that JWTs have valid structure). A truncated 5-field string that happens to produce 4 segments is silently accepted.

## Suggested fix

A few options:
1. **Validate JWT structure** in `Session.decode()` (check for 3 dot-separated base64 segments)
2. **Remove the 4-field fallback** if old-format sessions are no longer in use
3. **Add a version marker** to the session string format to distinguish old from new

## Environment

- atproto SDK version: 0.0.65
- Python: 3.12
- Discovered during integration testing of [atdata](https://github.com/forecast-bio/atdata)

issues.title: Strict datetime validation diverges from spec/reference on two edges: year 0000 and max length
issues.body:
Hi! I've been writing spec-conformance tests for an AT Protocol project I'm working on, and this SDK is what I cross-check my results against, as it's the most mature Python implementation of the protocol, so disagreeing with it is my cue to go digging. On two datetime edges we disagreed, and after arbitrating against the Lexicon spec and the reference `datetime.ts`, it turned out these look like rare cases where the divergence is on this side (same digging that surfaced [#695](https://github.com/MarshalX/atproto/pull/695) and [#696](https://github.com/MarshalX/atproto/pull/696)). Filing as an issue rather than a PR because the fix involves a design choice I didn't want to make for you.


**1. Year 0000 is rejected (spec lists it as a preferred valid example)**

```python
TypeAdapter(DateTime).validate_python('0000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', context={'strict_string_format': True})
# ValidationError: Invalid datetime: year 0 is out of range
```

The [Lexicon spec's valid examples](https://atproto.com/specs/lexicon#datetime) include `0000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` under "preferred", and the reference [`datetime.ts`](https://github.com/bluesky-social/atproto/blob/main/packages/syntax/src/datetime.ts) accepts years 0000–9999, rejecting only datetimes that normalize to a negative year (e.g. `0000-01-01T00:00:00+01:00`, which is in the interop invalid vectors). The root cause is structural: `validate_datetime` finishes with `datetime.fromisoformat`, and Python's `datetime.MINYEAR` is 1, so year 0000 can't even be represented. A fix probably means either special-casing year 0000 (e.g. substituting a stand-in leap year for the parse, plus an explicit check that an offset doesn't normalize below the year floor) or hand-rolling the semantic checks. Happy to send a PR for whichever direction you prefer, if any (in practice, this probably only bites by rejecting a joke post from year 0000 or something).

**2. No maximum length — a design question rather than a clear-cut bug**

The reference implementation rejects any datetime longer than 64 characters: [datetime.ts#L329-L330](https://github.com/bluesky-social/atproto/blob/20c5cc187aab538435c669c6e19a2d2f658af5f8/packages/syntax/src/datetime.ts#L329-L330). Unlike item 1, this rule appears nowhere in the Lexicon spec text — it exists only in the reference code — so it's genuinely your policy call: should strict mode here conform to the spec as written, or to the de-facto behavior of the network (which runs the reference)? Today `validate_datetime` has no length check at all, so e.g. a 65-char datetime with a 44-digit fractional-seconds part passes strict validation here but is rejected by the reference, and therefore by live PDS/relay/AppView infrastructure.

If you'd like to match the reference, the exact change I'd be happy to submit as a PR:

- `MAX_DATETIME_LENGTH: int = 64` alongside the other length constants in `string_formats.py`
- an early check in `validate_datetime`: `if len(v) > MAX_DATETIME_LENGTH: raise ValueError(...)` with a message mirroring the reference's ("too long (64 chars max)")
- parametrized tests pinning the 64/65-char boundary

One heads-up either way: adding the cap means strict mode starts rejecting over-long datetimes it currently accepts. That behavior change is exactly why I'm asking first rather than sending the PR directly.


Thanks again for the library!

issues.title: Proposal: score any external memory system with `evaluate_baselines.py --method precomputed`
issues.body:
The paper compares Memorilla with Mem0, MemoRAG, xRAG and LLMLingua-2, but the repo can only run closed book, RAG-k and full context. Anyone who wants to add a system today has to fork `evaluate_baselines.py`.

**Proposal.** One new method that reads each question's context from a file, with no new dependency:

```
python evaluate_baselines.py --benchmark all --method precomputed --contexts contexts.jsonl
```

One JSON object per line:

```json
{"benchmark": "triviaqa", "row": 0, "question": "<the split's question>", "contexts": ["<text>", "..."]}
```

- `row` is the 0-based index in the evaluated split. `question` must match the split, so a file built against another revision fails at load time.
- Every row of each requested benchmark appears exactly once. An empty `contexts` list means closed book for that row.
- The contexts go into the user turn in the given order, the same way `rag` does. The prompt, front truncation, `context.json`, scoring and output layout stay as they are, under `results/.../precomputed/`.

The change stays small: the method value, a `load_contexts` validator next to `retrieve`, and CPU tests with a fake engine.

Two questions before we open a PR:

1. Is a PR along these lines welcome, and would you change the schema or the flag name?
2. Do you have the Mem0 / MemoRAG / xRAG baseline scripts from the paper? If you publish them, we would port them to this format.

Through source-code inspection or automated scanning, rather than use in a project

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import asyncio
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch

from deepagents.middleware.async_subagents import AsyncSubAgentMiddleware
from langgraph.runtime import Runtime


async def main():
    md = AsyncSubAgentMiddleware(async_subagents=[dict(name="worker", description="Check a report", graph_id="worker")])
    task = dict(task_id="child", thread_id="child", agent_name="worker", run_id="first", status="waiting",
                created_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", last_checked_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", last_updated_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")
    client = AsyncMock()
    client.runs.get.return_value = {"run_id": "first", "status": "success"}
    client.runs.list.return_value = [{"run_id": "resumed", "status": "success"}]
    client.threads.get.return_value = {"status": "interrupted", "interrupts": {"node": [{"id": "confirm", "value": "Use deepagents?"}]}}
    with patch("deepagents.middleware.async_subagents.get_client", return_value=client):
        update = await md.abefore_model({"async_tasks": {"child": task}, "messages": []}, Runtime())
    notices = (update or {}).get("messages", [])
    print("Notifications:", len(notices))
    assert len(notices) == 1 and "Use deepagents?" in str(notices[0]["content"])


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
Actual on 0.7.37: Notifications: 0 (AssertionError). Expected: Notifications: 1.
```

### Description

1. The parent observes a child waiting for the user on run A.
2. The user answers on the child thread. Run B starts and pauses with a different question before the parent polls again.
3. The parent polls. The child thread exposes the new interrupt, but the parent keeps run A and sends no notification to its model. An explicit `check_async_task` does return the new question, paired with the old run ID in the saved task record.

issues.title: Screenshot self-checks cannot see scroll-reveal content (opacity:0)
issues.body:
## Problem

Any page that reveals content on scroll is invisible to a screenshot-based self-check, and the agent has no way to know.

The pattern is everywhere: sections start at `opacity: 0` (or `translateY(24px)`) and an IntersectionObserver adds a class when they enter the viewport. A capture taken at load time, or a full-page capture that never scrolls, photographs those sections blank. The agent then either:

- reports a page as broken when the content is merely unobserved, or
- worse, reports a page as verified while having looked at empty boxes, because the screenshot "looked sparse but plausible".

Neither outcome is detectable from the tool result. There is no signal in a screenshot that says "this region exists but is currently at opacity 0", and the toolset has no way to ask.

The same class of bug applies to `prefers-reduced-motion` branches: a page that gates its animation on that media query cannot be checked in either direction, because nothing sets the media feature.

## Repro

```html
<section class="reveal">Case study copy that matters</section>
<style>
  .reveal { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .8s }
  .reveal.in { opacity: 1 }
</style>
<script>
  const io = new IntersectionObserver((es) => es.forEach((e) => {
    if (e.isIntersecting) e.target.classList.add("in");
  }));
  document.querySelectorAll(".reveal").forEach((el) => io.observe(el));
</script>
```

Navigate to the page, capture. The section is not in the image. Scroll to it, wait, capture again: now it is. Nothing in the first capture distinguishes "empty by design" from "not yet revealed".

A partial mitigation exists (emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and hope the page responds), but pages that only implement the observer branch ignore it, so it cannot be the only answer.

## Proposal

At capture time, on by default:

1. Scroll the page to the bottom in viewport-height steps with a short dwell, then return to the top and wait for transitions to finish, before the final capture. This triggers real observers instead of faking their state.
2. Emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` during the capture, and expose it as an explicit parameter for both settings so a page can be checked with and without motion.
3. Report what is still invisible after settling: elements with text content, non-zero box, computed `opacity < 0.15` or `visibility: hidden`. That turns a silent blind spot into a finding, which is the difference between a check and a ritual.

Point 3 is the important one. Settling reduces the false negatives; the report is what makes the remaining ones visible.

## Prior art

Implemented as part of a local plugin (`web-qa`): `page.emulate_media(reduced_motion="reduce")` at context creation, an async settle pass that walks the document, then a metrics pass returning `hiddenText: [{el, opacity}]` and `hiddenTextCount`. A fixture page with one deliberate `opacity: 0` paragraph and one deliberate overflow was used to confirm the checks fire: it reported `p.hidden@0` and `div.wide right=1400`, which is the negative control that a screenshot-only check cannot provide.

## Related

- #315 and #25909 describe agent-driven QA workflows that would inherit this blind spot if the capture primitive does not address it.

Environment: Windows 11, Hermes desktop, Chromium via Playwright with `channel="chrome"`.

issues.title: Support Responses API for models that reject Chat Completions
issues.body:
## What I am trying to do

Use a model that requires the Responses API through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. With `WAKU_PROVIDER=openai`, Waku currently always calls `chat.completions.create()`. Changing `WAKU_BASE_URL` changes the server, but does not select the API protocol.

## Reproduction

On commit `4b69b321324750f231fdfd72a83b38ad7301dcc3`, configure:

```dotenv
WAKU_PROVIDER=openai
WAKU_BASE_URL=https://www.packyapi.com/v1
WAKU_MODEL=gpt-6.1-sol
WAKU_SMALL_MODEL=gpt-6.1-sol
```

Set the endpoint's API key locally, start `uv run waku dashboard`, and send a message in Chat.

The endpoint returns HTTP 400:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "protocol_not_supported",
    "message": "模型 gpt-6.1-sol 不支持 chat completions 协议",
    "type": "packy_api_error"
  }
}
```

The message means that the selected model does not support the Chat Completions protocol. The request ID and credentials are omitted.

Setup: macOS, Python 3.14.5, OpenAI SDK 2.45.0. This is a concrete third-party endpoint reproduction; it is not a claim about every provider's model availability.

## Expected behavior

An explicit setting should let an OpenAI-compatible provider use `/responses` when its endpoint and selected models support that API. Existing Chat Completions and Anthropic behavior should keep working.

## Where this belongs

This extends the existing model-provider adapters. It does not require a new tool, prompt content, or changes to the loop's Messages interface.

I have implemented a small opt-in adapter locally using `WAKU_OPENAI_API=responses`. It converts requests, function calls and results, token usage, and streaming events to the existing interface. With `store=false`, it replays output items, including encrypted reasoning, rather than relying on server-side conversation storage.

Dashboard chat now works in my local setup. The implementation also has deterministic offline tests for tool round trips and streaming; those are separate from the live chat check. I would like to contribute it in a PR.

Related: #137 (model-picker compatibility) and #146 (GPT-5.6 tool calls on Chat Completions). This request is specifically about explicit Responses API support.

`test_the_judge_scores_the_zero_dollar_reply_below_the_bar` expects < 0.7 and gets 0.7.

The fixture's reply says "The research cost $0.00, because every call used a free preview." The tool output the judge reads shows `"endpoint_id": "tomba.companies.similar"` with `"cost_usd": 0.0089`. Haiku scored `grounded: 9`, `addresses_question: 7`, and its note did not mention the cost:

> The assistant correctly identifies competitors using the tool outputs, but the categorization of which companies compete with which product (mem0 vs waku.one) lacks clear support in the tool results.

The rubric says "A claim the outputs contradict scores 0-3", and the judge did not apply it. Options:

- Make the rubric name costs and numbers explicitly: check every number in the reply, including what the turn cost, against the tool outputs.
- Judge with a stronger model than the provider's small model.

issues.title: Reflect fails on every call with gpt-oss on Bedrock since tool calls moved to a response schema (#6176)
issues.body:
## Summary

Since #6176 (every tool call goes through a response schema, `6c425f1b5`), every reflect fails when the reflect model is gpt-oss on Bedrock (`openai.gpt-oss-20b-1:0`, `openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0`). Reflect returns 500 on the first forced step:

```
LiteLLM returned invalid JSON after 4 attempts (finish_reason='tool_calls', content='')
[reflect_tool_call] reply did not follow the response schema: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Reflect tool-calling failure in bank ...: Reflect needs a model that follows a response schema, but bedrock/openai.gpt-oss-20b-1:0 produced no usable call during initial tool selection (iteration=1, tool_choice='search_mental_models', finish_reason='stop'). The model returned no content.
```

Before #6176 (native tool calling), the same models complete most reflects.

## Cause

The schema turn sends no `tools`, but the prompt still describes the functions (`as_text_messages`) and asks for a call by name (`turn_request`). Given that, gpt-oss on Bedrock answers with a **native tool call** named after the described function. It returns `finish_reason='tool_calls'`, the arguments sit in `tool_calls`, and `content` is empty. The schema path only parses `content`, so every attempt counts as "no usable call".

Direct LiteLLM (1.104.0) calls with the real first-turn reflect prompt (the `search_mental_models` forced step). Each row is 2 runs with `reasoning_effort` low and 2 runs unset; all runs gave the same result:

| model | request | finish_reason | content | tool_calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b | `response_format` json_schema (default) | `tool_calls` | empty | `search_mental_models` |
| gpt-oss-120b | `response_format` json_schema (default) | `tool_calls` | empty | `search_mental_models` |
| gpt-oss-20b | schema in prompt (`HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_IN_PROMPT=true`) | `stop` | empty | none |
| gpt-oss-120b | schema in prompt | `stop` | valid JSON args | none |

So `STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_IN_PROMPT` is a workaround for 120b only. 20b returns nothing at all (its reasoning says it "needs to call search_mental_models", and then the call is dropped because no tools are declared).

## End-to-end comparison

Reflect with gpt-oss on Bedrock as the reflect model (retain and consolidation on a fixed model), on the same helpdesk-style bank and question set, 25–75 reflects per row:

| reflect model | before #6176 | after #6176 |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b | ~12% errors | 100% errors |
| gpt-oss-120b | ~1% errors | 100% errors |
| Claude Haiku 4.5 (Bedrock) | 0% errors | 0% errors |

## Suggested fix

In the schema path, when `content` is empty and the reply carries native `tool_calls` whose name matches a declared tool (the forced tool on a named turn), take the call from `tool_calls` and validate its arguments against the held schema as if they had come in `content`. Some models emit a call whenever a function is described, whatever the request declares, so this is safer than relying on the prompt to stop them.

A regression test could feed a provider reply with `finish_reason='tool_calls'`, empty content and one matching tool call through the schema turn, and check that it yields that call.

issues.title: CLI `retain-files` uses filename stem as document_id, so same-named files in different folders overwrite each other
issues.body:
### Bug Description

`hindsight memory retain-files <bank> <dir>` walks the directory recursively (the default), but sends only each file's basename. `ApiClient::file_retain` then sets `document_id` to the filename stem. Files in different folders that share a stem (`a/README.md`, `b/README.md`, `c/README.pdf`) all get `document_id = "README"`, so each later upload replaces the earlier document.

Nothing warns, and the command reports success. The relative path is never sent, so the server can't tell the files apart or recover them. No flag overrides this: `retain-files` only exposes `--context`, `--strategy`, `--async` and `--recursive`. There is no document-id, tags or metadata option.

The same collision also happens inside one folder when two files differ only by extension (`notes.md` and `notes.pdf`).

Code, at v1.2.1 (main is the same):

- Basename only: [`hindsight-cli/src/commands/memory.rs` L624-L629](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/0eb02d8c418eac6b489bc63883c993b2257dfac4/hindsight-cli/src/commands/memory.rs#L624-L629)
- Stem as `document_id`: [`hindsight-cli/src/api.rs` L369-L375](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/0eb02d8c418eac6b489bc63883c993b2257dfac4/hindsight-cli/src/api.rs#L369-L375)
- Recursive walk: [`hindsight-cli/src/commands/memory.rs` L586-L596](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/0eb02d8c418eac6b489bc63883c993b2257dfac4/hindsight-cli/src/commands/memory.rs#L586-L596)

Scale: in a ~1,100-file markdown notes folder, 216 files share 50 stems (`README`, `summary`, `PLAN`, ...), so one `retain-files` run would overwrite 166 documents.

### Steps to Reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p demo/a demo/b && cd demo
echo one > a/README.md
echo two > b/README.md
hindsight memory retain-files mybank .
```

Then list the bank's documents.

### Expected Behavior

Two documents, one per file, each identifiable by its path relative to the walked root.

### Actual Behavior

One document, `README`. The second upload replaces the first, and `a/README.md`'s content is gone.

### Suggested fix

- Derive `document_id` from the path relative to the walked root (e.g. `a/README.md`), or put this behind a flag such as `--doc-id-from-path` if keeping the current ids matters for existing users.
- Detect duplicate `document_id`s within a single run and warn or fail before uploading.
- Send the relative path in metadata (e.g. `metadata.path`). The Obsidian integration already does this with vault-relative paths ([`sync.ts` L116-L118, L171](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/0eb02d8c418eac6b489bc63883c993b2257dfac4/hindsight-integrations/obsidian/src/sync.ts#L116-L118)).

### Version

hindsight-cli v1.2.1 (code unchanged on main)

issues.title: hermes: _managed_uvx_dir ignores HERMES_HOME, so the managed uvx is never found on Windows
issues.body:
### Bug Description

`_managed_uvx_dir()` in `hindsight-integrations/hermes/embedded.py` only looks in `Path.home() / ".hermes" / "tools"` and `Path(sys.prefix).parent / "tools"`. On Windows neither exists. Hermes keeps its home in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` there (`get_hermes_home()` uses `HERMES_HOME` if set, otherwise `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` on win32 and `~/.hermes` elsewhere), and its tools live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\tools\uv-*\`. The plugin runs from a venv under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\installs\<hash>\environments\<hash>\venv`, so `sys.prefix.parent` is an environment folder with no `tools` directory.

The result is that the #5192 fallback finds nothing and the daemon fails with `Command not found: uvx`, even though `uvx.exe` is sitting in Hermes's own tools folder. The same hardcoded path would affect anyone running Hermes with a custom `HERMES_HOME` on Linux or macOS.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows 11, Hermes installed with its package manager, default home (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`), no `uvx` on PATH.
2. Install the hindsight plugin, set `local_embedded` mode.
3. Run any memory operation so the daemon starts.

Check from the Hermes environment:

```python
import os, shutil
from pathlib import Path
tools = Path(os.environ["HERMES_HOME"]) / "tools"
print([shutil.which("uvx", path=str(p)) for p in tools.glob("uv-*")])   # finds uvx.EXE
print((Path.home() / ".hermes" / "tools").exists())                      # False
```

### Expected Behavior

The managed `uvx` is found whatever the Hermes home is. Resolving the home through `HERMES_HOME` (falling back to `~/.hermes`) would cover it. Asking Hermes's `pm.install.uv_launcher` would too, as suggested in #5580.

### Actual Behavior

```
Command not found: uvx
Full command: uvx hindsight-api@1.2.1 --idle-timeout 300 --port 9177
RuntimeError: Failed to start the Hindsight daemon for profile 'hermes'
```

I changed the first tuple entry to `Path(os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME") or Path.home() / ".hermes") / "tools"`. That alone was not enough, because with hindsight-embed 1.2.x the direct `ensure_running()` branch never calls `_managed_uvx_dir`. That is #6451. With both changes the daemon started and the first retain completed.

One more thing I hit on that first start: downloading `hindsight-api` and its dependencies (about 3.9 GB in the uv cache) took longer than the daemon manager's 180 s startup wait. Each attempt timed out and restarted the download. Running `uvx hindsight-api@1.2.1 --help` by hand to fill the cache fixed it. I can split this into its own issue if you prefer.

### Version

Hindsight plugin 1.2.4, hindsight-embed 1.2.1, Hermes on Python 3.14.9, Windows 11.

### LLM Provider

github-copilot (not related to this bug).

issues.title: Flaky: test_a_second_restore_into_the_same_fresh_bank_is_refused accepts only one of the two refusal messages
issues.body:
## What happens

`tests/test_bank_restore_race.py::test_a_second_restore_into_the_same_fresh_bank_is_refused[without-config]` fails now and then in CI (seen on PR #6525, `test-api (1/3)`, then green on the rerun):

```
AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match.
 Expected regex: 'created by another restore'
 Actual message: "Target bank 'race-dst-…' already exists; import-bank restores into a fresh bank (it is not a merge). …"
```

## Why

Two restores race into the same fresh bank. Depending on timing, the second one is refused either by the "already exists" check before it starts, or by the "created by another restore" check while it runs. Both refuse it, which is the behaviour the test is about, but the test only accepts the second message.

## What should happen

Assert the refusal, not which of the two checks fired, e.g. `match="created by another restore|already exists"`. Or force the interleaving so only one path can happen.

## Where

`hindsight-api-slim/tests/test_bank_restore_race.py`, from #6408.

issues.title: hindsight-embed: CLI install path uses `bash -c "curl … | bash"` with text=True — UnicodeDecodeError on Windows, and get-cli has no Windows branch, so every forwarded command fails
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, every `hindsight-embed` command that forwards to the CLI (`memory retain`, `memory recall`, `bank list`, even `--version`) fails, because the "install the CLI" step is a POSIX shell pipeline.

`hindsight_embed/daemon_client.py:205-211`:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["bash", "-c", f"curl -fsSL {CLI_INSTALLER_URL} | bash"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,        # no encoding= → locale codec (cp936/GBK) on Windows
    env=env,
)
```

Two independent defects:

1. **`text=True` without `encoding=`.** The reader thread decodes the installer's output with the console codec and dies:
   `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 383` (raised in `subprocess._readerthread`). `result.stdout`/`result.stderr` are then never populated, so the wrapper can only report a bare `CLI installation failed (exit code 1)` with no diagnostics.
2. **The installer has no Windows branch.** `https://hindsight.vectorize.io/get-cli` is POSIX-only: its `uname -s` case matches `Darwin` and `Linux` only (205 lines, no `MINGW`/`MSYS`/`CYGWIN`/`Windows_NT`, no `.exe`, no PowerShell). So even with the decoding fixed, the step cannot install on Windows — despite #5258 publishing native Windows x64 CLI binaries.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (build 26300); git-bash present on PATH, so `bash` resolves and `"bash", "-c"` does run
- Node v24.19.0, npm 12.1.0
- `hindsight-embed` 1.2.1 (via `uvx hindsight-embed@latest`)

## Steps to reproduce

```
hindsight-embed -p coding-agent memory retain ov-test "hello"
```

Output:

```
Exception in thread Thread-2 (_readerthread):
  ...
  File "subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
    buffer.append(fh.read())
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 383: illegal multibyte sequence
CLI installation failed (exit code 1):
Installing hindsight CLI (version 1.2.1)...
  Installer URL: https://hindsight.vectorize.io/get-cli
```

`PYTHONUTF8=1` / `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` do not help — switching the codec only changes the error to `'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xc0`, because the installer writes non-UTF-8 bytes. On a machine without `bash` on PATH the same branch fails earlier with a caught `FileNotFoundError` and the same generic message.

## Impact

The CLI is the documented surface for `memory retain/recall/reflect`, `bank list`, `daemon logs` and `ui *`. On Windows all of those are unusable, and the daemon being healthy and reachable on `127.0.0.1:9077` does not help. The only working surface is the HTTP API directly.

## Suggested fixes

1. On Windows, install through PowerShell (`powershell -NoProfile -Command "irm <url> | iex"`) or `Invoke-WebRequest`, rather than `bash -c`
2. Always pass `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"` alongside `text=True` (the same class of bug was already fixed in #3747, #3837 and #4344)
3. When the CLI genuinely cannot be installed on a platform, say so explicitly ("the bundled CLI installer does not support Windows; use the HTTP API") instead of reporting an exit code

## Workaround

Talk to the daemon over HTTP:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9077/v1/default/banks/<bank>/memories \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":[{"content":"..."}]}'
```

and start the control plane with `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-control-plane`.

issues.title: TLP completion retirement trusts completer-controlled byte_count: early tag reuse cross-corrupts requests; oversized value wedges DMA permanently (BCM flag decoded but unused)
issues.body:
## Description

In `litepcie/tlp/`, a completion's retirement is driven by completer-controlled header fields. `depacketizer.py:439` computes

```python
end = length == byte_count[2:]
```

where `length` (CplD header DW0) and `byte_count` (DW1) are both written by the completer. A completion whose `byte_count[2:]` happens to equal its `length` on a non-final TLP asserts `end` on that TLP's last beat: the request retires after partial delivery, its tag returns to the free pool and is reissued to a **new** request — and the remaining beats of the old completion (still arriving under the same tag) demux into the new request's buffer and are delivered on the new request's stream, with the new request's `channel`/`user_id`.

The PCIe spec defines **BCM (Byte Count Mismatch)** for exactly this anomaly; `tlp/common.py:153` decodes it, but the flag is not consumed anywhere. There is also no timeout anywhere in the TLP layer (`grep -rn timeout litepcie/tlp litepcie/frontend/dma.py litepcie/core` → nothing), and the demux (`controller.py:149-151`) checks neither whether a tag is currently outstanding nor completer/requester ID.

## Two failure modes (both reproduced in simulation)

**A — silent cross-request corruption (byte_count too small):** a 16-DW request receives a lying CplD (`length=4, byte_count=16`) → `end=(4==4)=1` → retires after 1 of 4 beats; the tag is reissued; the stale 12-DW continuation then arrives under the same tag and is **delivered on the new request's stream** — the new request retires on foreign dwords, followed by a spurious `first=1` mid-stream (reorder desync).

**B — permanent DMA hang (byte_count too large):** all 16 requested DW delivered but `byte_count=0xffc` → `end=(16==1023)=0` → zero end beats, tag never recycled, `req_queue` head-of-line blocks, reorder buffers fill, RX path wedges; 512-cycle soak shows no recovery. No watchdog exists.

Control test (truthful CplD) behaves correctly — both failures come solely from completer-supplied header fields.

## Threat model

The completer of the endpoint's MRd: trusted in the classic RC model, but this also fires from a **buggy** RC/completer whose byte-count bookkeeping errs — which is why PCIe defines BCM. In P2P/switch topologies the demux additionally trusts small sequential tags (0..N-1) with no outstanding-status check.

## Suggested directions

- retire on *requested* length (per-tag expected-DW ledger filled at request issue), not the completer's byte_count;
- consume the already-decoded BCM flag (discard/flag mismatched completions);
- validate tags against the outstanding set on demux;
- a completion watchdog for the wedge case.

Repro testbench (real `LitePCIeTLPDepacketizer` + `LitePCIeTLPController`, genuine CplD TLP injection so `end` is computed by the path under test) available — happy to attach or send a PR with the retirement-ledger fix + regressions.

issues.title: phy/s7ddrphy/usddrphy: DQS preamble/postamble not generated (FIXME), DQS toggles through the extra OE cycles
issues.body:
## Observation

In `litedram/phy/s7ddrphy.py` (lines 446-447) and `litedram/phy/usddrphy.py` (lines 265-266), the
`DQSPattern` preamble/postamble inputs are commented out:

```python
dqs_pattern   = DQSPattern(
    #preamble      = dqs_preamble,  # FIXME
    #postamble     = dqs_postamble, # FIXME
    ...
```

The same `dqs_preamble`/`dqs_postamble` signals still extend the DQS output-enable
(`dqs_oe_delay.input.eq(dqs_preamble | dqs_oe | dqs_postamble)`), so DQS is driven for one extra
sys_clk cycle before and after each write burst, but `DQSPattern.o` stays at the default
`0b0101...` toggling pattern for those cycles. On the wire, DQS keeps toggling through the
preamble/postamble windows instead of the JEDEC shapes:

- write preamble (DDR3: tWPRE, about 1 tCK low before the first rising edge; DDR4: 1 or 2 tCK),
- write postamble (tWPST, about 0.5 tCK low after the last falling edge, then high-Z).

`DQSPattern` already has preamble/postamble patterns (`utils.py`), but they are written for a
16-bit pattern and were presumably disabled because they did not line up with the bitslip/OSERDES
mapping (8 bits used at 1:4, 4 bits at 1:2).

## Risks

- Extra DQS edges before the burst: the DRAM may latch data early if the edges fall inside its
  tDQSS window; write leveling hides most of it today (the extra toggles are before the
  aligned edge), but margins shrink with tDQSS and with multi-rank/RDIMM loads.
- Extra edges after the burst (postamble): can be counted as data strobes by some devices,
  and the DQS line does not settle low before tristating (ringing on the next turnaround,
  ODT interaction).
- Behaviour differs from the vendor PHYs, so a module that works with MIG may fail with LiteDRAM
  at higher frequencies.

## What to check on hardware

1. Scope DQS/DQ (or a LiteScope capture of `dqs_pattern.o`, `dqs_oe_delay.output`) on a write
   burst: count the DQS edges per burst (should be BL8 = 4 rising edges plus the preamble shape).
2. Enable the preamble/postamble patterns with a pattern adapted to 8 (1:4) and 4 (1:2) bits,
   rerun write leveling + `sdram_cal` + memtest across a sys_clk sweep (`bench/*.py --test`) and
   compare the passing windows with the current code.
3. Check DDR4 (usddrphy) with 1 tCK and 2 tCK write preamble settings (MR4).

Boards to cover: one 7-Series DDR3 (Arty/KC705), one 7-Series DDR2 1:2 (Nexys4DDR), one
UltraScale DDR4 (KCU105) and one UltraScale+ (XCU1525).


Found during the review of the LiteDRAM manual (Claude Code, supervised by Florent Kermarrec).

issues.title: phy/s7ddrphy: DFI built with max(4, nphases) phases while settings declare nphases=2 (DDR2 1:2)
issues.body:
## Observation

`litedram/phy/s7ddrphy.py:299`:

```python
self.dfi = dfi = Interface(addressbits, bankbits, nranks, 2*databits, max(4, nphases))
```

At DDR2 1:2 (`nphases=2`) the PHY's DFI has 4 phases while `self.settings.nphases == 2`. This was
added in f537b5d ("phy/s7ddrphy: Fix DDR2 case.") because the serializers index the DFI with a
hard-coded 8-bit mapping (`dfi.phases[n//2] for n in range(8)` for commands, DQ, DM, read data),
so phases 2/3 must exist even though OSERDESE2 uses `DATA_WIDTH = 2*nphases = 4` (D1-D4 only).

## Risks

- Anything that trusts `len(phy.dfi.phases)` instead of `settings.nphases` sees 4 phases:
  `get_standard_names()` (exported DFI ports of a standalone/external controller), DFI
  monitors/analyzers, rate converters, tests.
- The controller/DFII side is built from `settings.nphases=2`; `Record.connect` connects
  p0/p1 only and phases 2/3 stay at their reset values (NOPs). This is fine today, but any change
  that drives phases 2/3 (or reads their `rddata_valid`) silently does nothing at 1:2.
- Read data on phases 2/3 is driven from deserializer bits that do not exist at DATA_WIDTH=4.

## Proposal

Build the DFI with `nphases` and make the serializer mappings depend on `2*nphases` bits
(`range(2*nphases)`, `D{n+1}` for `n < 2*nphases`), so the DFI matches the settings. Add a test
that checks `len(phy.dfi.phases) == phy.settings.nphases` for every PHY/rate.

## What to check on hardware

DDR2 1:2 on a Nexys4DDR (A7DDRPHY): BIOS calibration, `sdram_test`/memtest and a bench sweep
(`bench/*.py --test`) before/after, plus a DDR3 1:4 board to confirm no regression.


Found during the review of the LiteDRAM manual (Claude Code, supervised by Florent Kermarrec).
