- [ ] **ProRes line, 8-bit source, `overlay --image`** still composites through RGB.
- [ ] **Text-default pictographs above U+1F300** (e.g. 🌡) are still counted as emoji; an emoji placeholder inside an italic cue ends with `{\r}`, so the text after it loses its italics.
- [ ] **A truncated source reads as fine in 22 of 25 tools** (`tests/sweep.py` on a one-third MKV): #424's class.

issues.title: audio.py --limit: alimiter without latency=1 delays the output by the look-ahead
issues.body:
**What happens.** `audio.py --limit` uses `alimiter` without `latency=1`, so the output is delayed by the look-ahead (5 ms by default; 239 samples at 48 kHz) and drifts against the picture.

**Effect downstream.** A consumer that must hit a loud target under a true-peak ceiling (e.g. -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP from a peaky master) cannot use the limiter without an A/V offset, so it has to refuse the job instead.

**Proposed fix.** Set `latency=1` (latency compensation), or add a true-peak limiter stage to `loudness.py`, and state the resulting delay (zero) in the result.

issues.title: Multitrack audio delivery: write several audio files as one WAV / MOV with named tracks
issues.body:
**Request.** A tool that takes several audio files (e.g. dialogue / music / effects stems, or per-language tracks) and writes them as one multitrack file: a multichannel/multi-stream WAV, or a MOV with one audio stream per input, each with a track name / language tag, sample-exact and with lengths verified.

**Why.** Broadcast and NLE deliveries often require stems or language tracks in one file. audio-production-skill now exports stems as separate files (STEMS, ADR-24), but cannot offer the single-file form because ffmpeg-skill has no way to write it.

issues.title: audio.py pad/trim rounds lengths to the millisecond (up to 24 samples off at 48 kHz)
issues.body:
**What happens.** `audio.py` pads/trims with `atrim=0:{dur:.3f}`, i.e. rounded to the millisecond. When the programme length is not a whole number of milliseconds, the result is up to 24 samples (48 kHz) longer or shorter than the target.

**Effect downstream.** Stems that must sum exactly to the mix have to be the same sample count as the programme; audio-production-skill now detects the mismatch and refuses (`stem_length_mismatch`).

**Proposed fix.** Trim and pad in samples: `atrim=end_sample=N` and `apad=whole_len=N`, with N taken from the target length at the output sample rate. Same family as #455 / #468 (millisecond rounding in join.py).

issues.title: join (3.6.3) on FFmpeg 8.0.1: H.264+AAC MP4 join returns a clip 3 frames short
issues.body:
**What happens.** With ffmpeg-skill main 3.6.3 (#473, whole-frame join lengths) and FFmpeg 8.0.1 (GitHub runner), video-editing-skill PUNCH_IN, which does a cut, then crop/scale, then a join of three H.264+AAC MP4 parts at 30 fps, returns a clip 3 frames (0.100 s) shorter than its input: 7.066016 s vs 7.166341 s by ffprobe format duration.

**Where it reproduces.**
- FFmpeg 8.0.1 with ffmpeg-skill 3.6.3: fails.
- FFmpeg 6.1.1 with ffmpeg-skill 3.6.3: lengths are equal (7.166667 s).
- FFmpeg 8.0.1 with ffmpeg-skill v2.24.1: passes.

Seen in video-production-agent integration (`VideoEditingFeaturesRealTests.test_punch_in_keeps_frame_and_duration`), on main too (run 43250013018).

**Likely scope.** This looks like the H.264+AAC MP4 case that #475 leaves open. #473's "FFmpeg 7.1 / 8 in CI" item is still unchecked; adding FFmpeg 8 to CI would catch it.

issues.title: background-model config change is never retried when its spec rebuild fails
issues.body:
## What happens

A change to `agent.role_models.background` must rewrite the lite and heartbeat agent specs, which carry that model. Its applier, `_apply_background_model` in `src/kiro_crew/dashboard/server_runtime/config_watch.py`:

- catches any rebuild exception, logs a warning and returns normally;
- calls `rebuild_agent_config`, which cannot say whether it wrote anything, so a rebuild that wrote nothing (the existing spec could not be read) is logged as "background agent specs rebuilt".

`ConfigWatch` retries only an applier that raises, so in both cases the saved value never reaches those specs until a restart. Settings and `config.json` show the new model while the specs keep the old pin, with no notice.

The sibling `agent.model` applier already handles this: it uses `rebuild_agent_config_reporting` and raises on `wrote=False`, and its tests pin that.

## Expected

A rebuild that fails, or writes nothing this instance could have written, defers for retry. A config save still answers 200.

## Proof

With the rebuild stubbed to raise or to return `wrote=False`, the applier on main returns without raising.

issues.title: Allow Bot Groups (similar to Session Folders)
issues.body:
## What

Let users put Bots into Groups, much like Sessions can be put into Folders. A Group should support:

- Hierarchy: Groups can nest, and each level can expand and collapse in the Bots sidebar.
- Default settings for new Bots created in that Group (for example model, approval mode, check-ins, project directory).
- Moving a Bot between Groups, and leaving a Bot ungrouped.

The Sessions page should show this too. Bot sessions should appear under their Group, instead of in the current flat, ungrouped list of Bot sessions at the bottom.

Groups should be their own concept, not reused Folders. Folders have different properties (they group chats by project/topic), so a shared grouping would mix two models.

## Why

With more than a handful of Bots, the flat list gets hard to scan. Related Bots (for example several Bots for one team or project) can't be kept together, and every new Bot has to be set up from scratch even when it should share settings with its siblings. On the Sessions page, all Bot sessions pile up at the bottom with no structure.

## Additional Context

- Related: #35647 (expand/collapse toggle for the Bot sidebar), #35646 (hover menu on Bot rows), #33208 (hiding the Bots row and starred Bots).
- Suggested labels for triage: enhancement, area for Bots/sidebar UI.

issues.title: Download succeeds but request returns 500 when the torrent URL redirects to a magnet link
issues.body:
## Environment

- AudioBookRequest v1.10.5, official Docker image `markbeep/audiobookrequest:1`
- Prowlarr 2.x with torrent indexers (observed with a Knaben result whose grab resolves to a RuTracker magnet)

## Symptom

Starting a download returns HTTP 500 to the user even though the grab itself succeeded: Prowlarr accepts the release and the torrent shows up in the download client. Because the handler dies mid-way, the book is never marked downloaded, no success notification is sent, and the ABS scan is not triggered.

## What happens

After a successful grab, `start_download` fetches the source's `download_url` to extract the torrent info hash for notification metadata (`app/internal/prowlarr/prowlarr.py:123`, calling `_get_torrent_info_hash` at `prowlarr.py:39`). For some indexers, Prowlarr's proxied download URL responds with a redirect to a `magnet:` URI. aiohttp refuses to follow non-HTTP redirects and raises, and the exception propagates out of the whole request:

```
File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 878, in _request
    raise NonHttpUrlRedirectClientError(r_url)
aiohttp.client_exceptions.NonHttpUrlRedirectClientError: magnet:?xt=urn:btih:<infohash-redacted>&tr=http%3A%2F%2Fbt.t-ru.org%2Fann%3Fmagnet
```

Note the irony: the info hash the code wanted is right there in the magnet URI it crashed on.

## Reproduction

1. Add an indexer whose torrent downloads resolve to magnet redirects (e.g. Knaben results that proxy RuTracker items).
2. Request a book and start a download for such a source.
3. The torrent is added to the download client, but the request returns 500 and the book stays "not downloaded".

## Suggested direction

- In `_get_torrent_info_hash`, request with `allow_redirects=False`; if the response is a redirect to a `magnet:` URI, parse the info hash from it (the same parsing already exists for `magnet_url` sources at `prowlarr.py:127-131`).
- Regardless, wrap the metadata fetch in a try/except so a failure to enrich notification metadata can never fail a download that already succeeded.

issues.title: Maximise app performance: startup, inference, memory, long jobs, UI, install, energy, mobile
issues.body:
Tracking issue: make VoiceStudio measurably faster and lighter across every dimension users feel, on macOS, Windows and Linux (and phones). Each item lands as a focused PR with a before/after number. No regression in output quality or cross-platform behaviour (CLAUDE.md parity rule: acceleration may vary by host, features may not).

## Dimensions

**1. App startup**
- [ ] Measure cold and warm time to first paint and to "backend ready" on each OS
- [ ] Lazy-load heavy routes and engines; defer non-critical IPC and checks until after first paint
- [ ] Trim the backend's import-time work (`_phase_a_build_inner`) and import routers on demand

**2. Inference throughput and latency**
- [ ] Per-engine benchmark (time to first audio, real-time factor) on CUDA, MPS, ROCm, Vulkan and CPU
- [ ] Keep models warm between takes; avoid redundant reloads on settings changes
- [ ] Stream the first chunk early for TTS and dictation; batch chunks where engines allow
- [ ] Use fp16/bf16, quantised (GGUF) and `torch.compile` paths where the host supports them, skipped cleanly where not

**3. Memory (RAM and VRAM)**
- [ ] Profile peak RAM and VRAM per engine and per pipeline (dub, long-form, batch)
- [ ] Unload idle engines and free caches under memory pressure; one engine resident by default
- [ ] Stop holding long audio fully in memory; stream to disk

**4. Long jobs (dubbing, audiobooks, 50-video batches)**
- [ ] Pipeline overlap: ASR, translation and TTS stages run concurrently where safe
- [ ] Resume from the last finished segment after a crash or restart
- [ ] Bounded parallelism tuned to the device instead of fixed

**5. UI responsiveness**
- [ ] Renderer bundle size budget and code splitting; track it in CI
- [ ] Virtualise long lists (history, voices, projects, gallery)
- [ ] Keep the main and renderer threads free: no sync IPC or heavy work on render paths
- [ ] Interaction latency budget (e.g. < 100 ms for clicks) checked by the UI crawler

**6. Install, update and disk**
- [ ] Smaller installers and runtime (prune unused wheels and assets)
- [ ] Faster first-run setup: parallel downloads within the sanctioned endpoints, better resume
- [ ] Differential updates where the updater supports them
- [ ] Shared model caches without duplicates; show and clean disk use

**7. Energy and thermals**
- [ ] Idle CPU near zero: no polling loops while idle; back off background checks
- [ ] Battery-aware defaults on laptops

**8. Mobile (on-device)**
- [ ] On-device model load time and memory on mid-range Android and iPhone
- [ ] Quantised on-device models; keep the UI at 60 fps during generation

## Measurement
- [ ] Add a reproducible benchmark script (`scripts/bench/`) with fixed inputs, run per platform
- [ ] Record baselines for the current release in this issue, then compare each PR against them
- [ ] Add CI perf smoke checks for startup time, bundle size and idle CPU, with alert thresholds that don't block merges on noise

## Rules
- Local-first unchanged: no new network calls for telemetry. Opt-in Supermetry analytics may carry coarse, content-free timing only if allowlisted in `backend/core/analytics.py`.
- No output-quality regressions: fixed-seed audio comparisons for engine changes.
- On-disk model state stays compatible (no forced reinstalls).

issues.title: chore(tooling): review the S110 waivers in the expert scripts
issues.body:
PR #371 turns on ruff S110: an `except` (bare, `Exception` or `BaseException`) whose body is only `pass` fails `pnpm lint:py`. A swallowed error lets a run report success.

The expert scripts that predate the rule keep a per-file waiver in `ruff.toml`, with their count of hits. This issue tracks removing them.

## Per site

- Fix it: catch the narrowest exception, then log, re-raise, or record the failure in the result.
- Or keep it: add `# noqa: S110` and the reason on the `except` line, when the host application's error is safe to ignore there.
- A comment beside the `pass` does not satisfy S110.

- Remove the file's `[lint.per-file-ignores]` entry once every clause is fixed or carries a reason.

issues.title: Notes batch actions report full success after rejected archive/delete requests
issues.body:
AI-assisted bug report, reproduced against unchanged public dev `0276e15f6e2e7a4a692d130243f2a02c3f57ffe0` before implementing a fix.

### Environment

Native macOS/Python 3.12/Uvicorn/SQLite, authenticated disposable account; Chrome at 1440×1000 and 390×844. No model inference, API response interception or DOM replacements.

### Reproduction

1. Create three owned notes. Enter Notes → Select, select all three and click Archive or Delete (confirm deletion).
2. Make the server reject just the middle note's mutation. I used a SQLite trigger in the disposable database to raise ABORT for that owned ID: `BEFORE DELETE ON notes`, or `BEFORE UPDATE OF archived ON notes WHEN NEW.archived=1`. The three actual HTTP responses are 200, 500, 200.
3. Observe the completion message, remaining note and selection.
4. For the same batch handling in reminder clearing, create three notes with past timed `due_date` values. Choose the Reminders filter and Clear past, confirming deletion, with the same middle-note rejection.

### Actual / expected

The app reports `Archived 3`, `Deleted 3` or `Cleared 3 past reminders`, shows no error and, for bulk selection, exits Select and clears the failed note's selection. The server correctly retains that note; only two operations succeeded. Failed items should be reported, successes counted accurately and failed selected notes kept available for retry.

Clearing the owned trigger allows a normal retry to succeed. This is client response handling, not a request to alter backend mutation/ownership rules. Individual note-delete error handling is a separate existing path.

### Source

`frontend/src/features/notes/application/selection.js` catches each rejected archive/delete request and then always reports the original count and exits selection. `application/deletion.js::_clearPastReminders` similarly ignores delete failures and claims every target was cleared. The deployed copies match.

### Duplicate checks

Searched open/closed issues and PRs for Notes bulk failures, rejected archive/delete, partial failure and clearing past reminders. No equivalent active fix found. Gallery draft-delete reporting and Skills rejected-write handling affect separate workflows; neither changes these Notes batch handlers.

issues.title: Inkling: BF16 router rounds distinct scores into ties before Top-K
issues.body:
`InklingTopkRouter` performs sigmoid and correction-bias addition in BF16 after `from_pretrained(..., dtype=torch.bfloat16)`. Distinct scores can become ties **before** Top-K, changing expert selection without producing NaNs. BF16 autocast also exposes this with FP32 model weights.

### System Info

- Transformers `5.23.0.dev0`, commit [b2556881](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/b25568817a6cb458f6d8b180a32698c2ab11fd26)
- Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`; reproduced on CPU and NVIDIA RTX A1000 Laptop GPU.
- Affected code: [InklingTopkRouter.forward](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/b25568817a6cb458f6d8b180a32698c2ab11fd26/src/transformers/models/inkling/modeling_inkling.py#L359-L379).

### Reproduction

No checkpoint download is needed. The logits below are exactly representable in BF16; the assertion excludes GEMM rounding as the cause.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers import InklingTextConfig
from transformers.models.inkling.modeling_inkling import InklingTopkRouter

device = "cpu"  # Also reproduces on CUDA.
config = InklingTextConfig(
    hidden_size=2, n_routed_experts=8, n_shared_experts=2,
    num_experts_per_tok=2,
)
router = InklingTopkRouter(config).to(device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
with torch.no_grad():
    router.weight.zero_()
    router.weight[:8, 0].copy_(
        torch.tensor([6.25, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8, 8.5, 9, 10], device=device)
    )
x = torch.tensor([[1., 0.]], device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
logits = F.linear(x, router.weight)
assert torch.equal(logits.float(), F.linear(x.float(), router.weight.float()))

print("BF16 scores:", logits.sigmoid()[0, :8].tolist())
print("Actual:", router(x)[2].sort().values.tolist())
for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
    scores = logits.to(dtype).sigmoid()[:, :8]
    print(dtype, scores.topk(2, sorted=False).indices.sort().values.tolist())
```

All eight BF16 sigmoid scores are `1.0`. Observed expert **sets**:

| Device | Current BF16 router | FP32 / FP64 sigmoid |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | `{5, 6}` | `{6, 7}` |
| CUDA | `{0, 1}` | `{6, 7}` |

Tie-breaking can vary; losing the distinct scores is the issue.

I also reproduced the loading path with a small three-layer `InklingForCausalLM` through `save_pretrained → from_pretrained(dtype=bfloat16)`. On CPU, switching to FP32 routing changed expert sets for 19/48 tokens while loss changed by only about `4.8e-7`; logits and gradients remained finite. This is a synthetic test, not a full-model quality measurement.

### Expected behavior

Preserve FP32 routing decisions, consistent with [SGLang's FP32-output gate projection](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/96f013b45202cabd8d4a0d6e79596f109538181e/python/sglang/srt/models/inkling_common/moe.py#L66-L120).

The locally tested fix needs three parts:

1. Disable autocast around FP32 projection, sigmoid, bias addition and normalization. Casting linear inputs/weights to `float()` alone still produces BF16 output under BF16 autocast.
2. Add `e_score_correction_bias` and `gate.global_scale` to `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict`. Loading currently rounds both to BF16; casting afterward cannot recover their values. Scope the scale entry to `gate` because dense MLPs have a same-named parameter.
3. Cast the final routing coefficients back to the hidden-state dtype, so the shared experts' BF16 down-projection remains compatible.

This approach passed CPU/CUDA forward/backward checks for BF16, BF16+AMP and FP32+AMP, plus exact FP32 bias/scale preservation across saving and loading.

Thanks for taking the time to review this. I'd appreciate your feedback on the diagnosis and proposed approach. I'll wait for your guidance before opening a PR, and I'd be happy to contribute the fix and regression tests.

issues.title: Default configs for 11 models can't build or run their own model (CohereCompass, DiffusionGemma, DeepseekOcr2, Granite4Vision, HunYuanVL, Moshi, PPOCRV6MediumDet, Qwen4Exp, Qwen3ASR, Molmo2, Step3p7)
issues.body:
### System Info

- `transformers` 5.23.0.dev0 (main @ `863d2620210d72fc0a9a03fdfe200bc9699154f6`)
- `torch` 2.12.1+cu130, Python 3.13, Linux x86_64

### Description

For 11 model families, a model built from its **default config** (`XConfig()`) either fails during `__init__` or builds but can never run a forward pass. The causes are a required field left as `None`, or two sub-config dimensions that disagree. Loading from the Hub works, because the checkpoint configs set these fields. The failures only show up when a model is built from the default config, as in tests, tiny-model construction, or `from_config` with partial overrides.

We found these while running every model class through `torch.compile` from default configs. As far as we could tell, none of them is tracked by an existing issue or PR. A related earlier case of the same kind: #43479 (Phi4Multimodal) and #42925 (TVP `type_vocab_size`).

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
import transformers as t

def build(model_cls, cfg_cls):
    try:
        cfg = getattr(t, cfg_cls)()
        with torch.device("meta"):
            getattr(t, model_cls)(cfg)
        return "OK"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:110]}"

for m, c in [
    ("CohereCompassModel", "CohereCompassConfig"),
    ("DiffusionGemmaModel", "DiffusionGemmaConfig"),
    ("DeepseekOcr2Model", "DeepseekOcr2Config"),
    ("Granite4VisionModel", "Granite4VisionConfig"),
    ("HunYuanVLModel", "HunYuanVLConfig"),
    ("MoshiForConditionalGeneration", "MoshiConfig"),
    ("PPOCRV6MediumDetModel", "PPOCRV6MediumDetConfig"),
    ("Qwen4ExpModel", "Qwen4ExpConfig"),
]:
    print(f"[build] {m}: {build(m, c)}")

c = t.Qwen3ASRConfig()
print(f"[dims] Qwen3ASR audio_config.output_dim={c.audio_config.output_dim} "
      f"text_config.hidden_size={c.text_config.hidden_size}")
c = t.Molmo2Config()
print(f"[dims] Molmo2 adapter_config.text_hidden_size={c.adapter_config.text_hidden_size} "
      f"text_config.hidden_size={c.text_config.hidden_size}")
c = t.Step3p7TextConfig()
print(f"[fwd] Step3p7 sliding_window={c.sliding_window} layer_types={sorted(set(c.layer_types))}")
```

Output:

```
[build] CohereCompassModel: KeyError: 'full_attention'
[build] DiffusionGemmaModel: TypeError: empty() received an invalid combination of arguments - got (tuple, dtype=NoneType, device=NoneType), but expec
[build] DeepseekOcr2Model: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
[build] Granite4VisionModel: TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
[build] HunYuanVLModel: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for ** or pow(): 'NoneType' and 'float'
[build] MoshiForConditionalGeneration: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'
[build] PPOCRV6MediumDetModel: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
[build] Qwen4ExpModel: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for //: 'NoneType' and 'NoneType'
[dims] Qwen3ASR audio_config.output_dim=3584 text_config.hidden_size=2048
[dims] Molmo2 adapter_config.text_hidden_size=3584 text_config.hidden_size=4096
[fwd] Step3p7 sliding_window=None layer_types=['full_attention']
```

### Per-model details

Where a public reference checkpoint exists, the value it uses is listed for comparison.

**A. The default config can't build the model**

| Model | Field left unset by the default | Where it fails | Reference checkpoint value |
|---|---|---|---|
| CohereCompass | `text_config.rope_parameters` defaults to `{}` with all-`full_attention` `layer_types`. The rotary init indexes `rope_parameters[layer_type]`. | `CohereCompassRotaryEmbedding.__init__` → `KeyError: 'full_attention'` | `CohereLabs/North-Micro-Vision-Instruct`: `{"sliding_attention": {...}, "full_attention": null}`, with mixed sliding/full layer types |
| DiffusionGemma | `text_config.num_experts`, `top_k_experts`, `moe_intermediate_size` are `None` | `DiffusionGemmaTextRouter`: `nn.Linear(hidden, None)` | `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`: 128 / 8 / 704 |
| DeepseekOcr2 | `text_config.mlp_layer_types` is `None` (also `n_group`, `topk_group`, `num_experts_per_tok`) | `DeepseekOcr2TextDecoderLayer.__init__`: `config.mlp_layer_types[layer_idx]` | `deepseek-community/DeepSeek-OCR-2`: `["dense"] + ["sparse"] * 11`, `n_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, `num_experts_per_tok=6` |
| Granite4Vision | `deepstack_layer_map` is `None` | `Granite4VisionModel.__init__`: `len(config.deepstack_layer_map)` | `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-3b-vision`: `[[-19, 9], [-13, 6], [-7, 3], [-1, 0]]`. Note that the `auto_docstring` checkpoint for this config points to `llava-hf/llava-v1.6-mistral-7b-hf`, which looks wrong. |
| HunYuanVL | `text_config.head_dim` is `None` | `HunYuanVLDenseV1Attention.__init__`: `self.head_dim**-0.5`. The config applies a `hidden_size // num_attention_heads` fallback in one place, but the attention module doesn't use it. | n/a (no `auto_docstring` checkpoint) |
| Moshi | top-level `audio_vocab_size` is `None` | `nn.Embedding(config.audio_vocab_size + 1, ...)`. This worked on 5.5.x, so it is a regression. | `kmhf/hf-moshika`: 2048 |
| PPOCRV6MediumDet | `intraclass_block_config` is `None` | `PPOCRV6MediumDetIntraclassBlock.__init__`: `intraclass_block_config["reduce_channel"]` | `PaddlePaddle/PP-OCRv6_medium_det_safetensors` (full dict in `config.json`) |
| Qwen4Exp | every `indexer_*` field is `None`, but each `indexed_attention` layer builds a `Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer` regardless | `Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer.__init__`: `token_budget // compress_ratio` | `Qwen/Qwen4-Exp` is gated, so we couldn't check |

**B. The model builds, but a forward pass can never succeed**

| Model | Inconsistency | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3ASR | `audio_config.output_dim=3584` but `text_config.hidden_size=2048` | The projector output is `masked_scatter`ed into the text embeddings, and `get_placeholder_mask` fails its numel check ("Audio features and audio tokens do not match, tokens: N, features: N") even when token counts match. |
| Molmo2 | `adapter_config.text_hidden_size=3584` but `text_config.hidden_size=4096` | Pooled image features are added onto the placeholder embeddings, and the numel check in `get_placeholder_mask` fails. |
| Step3p7 | `sliding_window=None`, and the default `layer_types` are all `full_attention` | `Step3p7TextModel.forward` always builds `create_sliding_window_causal_mask(...)` (`modeling_step3p7.py:892`), even when no layer uses sliding attention. This raises `ValueError: Could not find a sliding_window argument in the config, or it is not set`. |

### Expected behavior

`XModel(XConfig())` builds, and runs a forward pass on valid inputs, for every model class.

issues.title: finegrained_fp8 models are silently mis-dequantized when loaded on CPU if a quantized weight has partial blocks
issues.body:
### System Info ```text - transformers version: 5.22.1 - Platform: Linux-5.x-x86_64 (CPU-only) - Python version: 3.12.15 - Huggingface_hub version: 2.4.0 - Safetensors version: 0.8.0 - Accelerate version: 1.15.0 - PyTorch version: 2.15.0+cpu (CPU build) - CUDA/GPU: none — CPU-only host, which is exactly the forced-dequantize path ``` The same wrongness is bit-identical on transformers 5.17.0 (checked at the `Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one` level), and the relevant code is unchanged on current `main` (source-checked 2026-11-11: the equal-division derivation at ~L1152, the loud `ValueError` at ~L1148, and the partial-aware `_dequantize_fp8_weight` helper at ~L285 all coexist). ### Who can help? @SunMarc @MekkCyber (quantization) ### Reproduction Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. On a host **without GPU/XPU**, load a finegrained_fp8 checkpoint (`quant_method: "fp8"`, the DeepSeek checkpoint family) whose quantized linear weights have partial 128-blocks — i.e. any hidden/intermediate dimension that is not a multiple of `weight_block_size` (external per-block quantization tooling emits such ceil-shaped grids by construction). 2. transformers forces `dequantize=True` ("Using FP8 quantized models requires a GPU or XPU, we will default to dequantizing the model to bf16 since no GPU or XPU is available"), and `Fp8Dequantize` derives the block size from the scale grid **by equal division** (`block_m = rows // scale_rows`), while the format's semantics are ceil grids with partial edge blocks. 3. The load **succeeds silently** and the weights are wrong. On a GPU host the same checkpoint loads correctly (the quantized path's own `_dequantize_fp8_weight` is partial-block aware). Self-contained script (tiny locally generated Llama checkpoints in the DeepSeek fp8 format, no downloads; the same script is archived next to this issue as `issue-reproducer.py`): [issue-reproducer.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34669945/issue-reproducer.py) ```python import json import os import tempfile import warnings from pathlib import Path warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1") import torch from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM from transformers.integrations.finegrained_fp8 import ( Fp8Dequantize, _dequantize_fp8_weight, ) BLOCK, FP8_MAX = (128, 128), 448.0 def quantize_reference(w): """Quantize per the format's reference semantics (ceil grids).""" rows, cols = w.shape grid_r, grid_c = (rows + 127) // 128, (cols + 127) // 128 codes = torch.zeros_like(w) scales = torch.zeros(grid_r, grid_c) deq = torch.zeros_like(w) for i in range(grid_r): for j in range(grid_c): sl = (slice(i * 128, (i + 1) * 128), slice(j * 128, (j + 1) * 128)) mult = w[sl].abs().max().clamp(min=1e-12) / FP8_MAX codes[sl] = torch.clamp(w[sl] / mult, -FP8_MAX, FP8_MAX) scales[i, j] = mult # post-round truth: what any consumer reads back from the checkpoint deq[sl] = codes[sl].to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * mult return codes.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), scales, deq def build_checkpoint(root, hidden): torch.manual_seed(0) cfg = LlamaConfig(hidden_size=hidden, intermediate_size=512, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=4, vocab_size=128, max_position_embeddings=256, tie_word_embeddings=False, architectures=["LlamaForCausalLM"]) model = LlamaForCausalLM(cfg).to(torch.bfloat16) tensors, ground, qnames = {}, {}, [] for name, t in model.state_dict().items(): if name != "lm_head.weight" and any(s in name for s in ("q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj")): codes, scales, deq = quantize_reference(t.float()) prefix = name[: -len(".weight")] tensors[name], tensors[prefix + ".weight_scale_inv"] = codes, scales tensors[prefix + ".activation_scale"] = torch.tensor(1.0) ground[name] = deq qnames.append(name) else: tensors[name], ground[name] = t.detach().clone(), t d = root / f"ckpt-h{hidden}" d.mkdir(parents=True) save_file(tensors, str(d / "model.safetensors")) cd = cfg.to_dict() cd["quantization_config"] = {"quant_method": "fp8", "activation_scheme": "dynamic", "weight_block_size": [128, 128]} cd["torch_dtype"] = "bfloat16" (d / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(cd, indent=2, sort_keys=True)) return d, ground, qnames def load_and_compare(ckpt, ground, qnames): model = LlamaForCausalLM.from_pretrained(str(ckpt), torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) sd = model.state_dict() bad = 0 for n in qnames: bad += int((sd[n].float() - ground[n].to(torch.bfloat16).float()).abs().gt(0).sum()) return bad def main(): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td: root = Path(td) # control: every linear dim divisible by the 128 block d, g, q = build_checkpoint(root, 256) print("hidden 256 (divisible): wrong elements =", load_and_compare(d, g, q)) # defect: hidden 200 -> partial row blocks, grid (2, .), 200 % 2 == 0 d, g, q = build_checkpoint(root, 200) print("hidden 200 (partial): wrong elements =", load_and_compare(d, g, q)) # mechanism: the same codes+scales through both in-repo implementations t = load_file(str(d / "model.safetensors")) qn = next(n for n in q if n.endswith("q_proj.weight")) p = qn[: -len(".weight")] class _Q: class quantization_config: scale_fmt = "float" cpu = Fp8Dequantize(_Q())._dequantize_one(t[qn], t[p + ".weight_scale_inv"], output_dtype=torch.float32) helper = _dequantize_fp8_weight(t[qn], t[p + ".weight_scale_inv"], [128, 128], torch.float32) gt = g[qn] print("q_proj (200, 200), grid (2, 2):") print(" Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one (CPU load path): max diff", float((cpu - gt).abs().max())) print(" _dequantize_fp8_weight (partial-aware): max diff", float((helper - gt).abs().max())) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Actual output (transformers 5.22.1, CPU-only host): ```text [transformers] Using FP8 quantized models requires a GPU or XPU, we will default to dequantizing the model to bf16 since no GPU or XPU is available hidden 256 (divisible): wrong elements = 0 hidden 200 (partial): wrong elements = 168915 q_proj (200, 200), grid (2, 2): Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one (CPU load path): max diff 0.0129743292927742 _dequantize_fp8_weight (partial-aware): max diff 0.0 ``` All 14 quantized tensors of the `hidden_size=200` model are wrong (each 200×200 tensor has 10416/40000 wrong elements): rows 100–127 fall into the second derived block (100 rows each) although the quantizer's blocks were `[0:128] + [128:200]`, so they are dequantized with the wrong per-block scale. A second variant — a dimension whose size does not divide by its grid count — fails loudly instead (also wrong: the reference consumer loads such checkpoints fine):
ValueError from _dequantize_one (e.g. intermediate_size=131, weight (256, 131), grid (2, 2)) ```text File ".../transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py", line 1149, in _dequantize_one raise ValueError( ValueError: Weight shape (256, 131) not divisible by scale grid (2, 2). ```
Reference semantics for `weight_scale_inv` grids (why the above checkpoint is legal): vLLM's fp8 utils dequantizes with `repeat_interleave(block, ...)[:_N, :_K]` (partial-block aware), and transformers' own `_dequantize_fp8_weight` — used by the quantized path's backward in the same file — truncates `[..., :rows, :]` and handles a `rem` branch. Only the CPU forced-dequantize path assumes equal blocks. ### Expected behavior Loading the same fp8 checkpoint on a CPU-only host should produce the same weights as on a GPU host. Concretely, `Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one` should apply the ceil-grid block semantics grid cell `i` covers rows `[i*128, min((i+1)*128, rows)]` — exactly what `_dequantize_fp8_weight` already implements — instead of `block_m = rows // scale_rows`; and a scale grid inconsistent with `ceil(rows / weight_block_size[0])` should fail loudly rather than being reinterpreted by an arbitrary factorization (the current code accepts any grid that divides the shape, e.g. a `(1, 4)` grid for a 256×256 weight would silently use 64-column blocks).
